messages:

To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice cadence and contract questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency guarantees and the dedicated routing options. Procurement has asked me to confirm whether Redwood can support a quarterly invoicing cadence with Net-90 payment terms for the initial 12-month contract.

A few details:
- Our finance team prefers consolidated quarterly invoices to match their vendor schedule.
- They also request Net-90 for vendor onboarding to align with cashflow this quarter.
- We are planning a $180k ARR commitment in year one with a $30k implementation professional services milestone.

Are these payment terms something Redwood can accommodate? If so, what is the approval process? We may also need a simple SOW amendment and a PO reference.

Attaching our internal PO template (for reference).

Best,
Elena Morris
VP, Strategic Procurement
SpruceBridge

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice cadence and contract questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for outlining finance's preference. We're keen to move this forward.

Short answer: we can consider a conditional Net-90 / quarterly invoicing pilot for the first 3 quarters, but it requires executive signoff due to the cashf low and risk exposure. To put a proposal in front of deal desk / finance, I'll escalate with the following suggested mitigations:
- Require a PO + signed SOW amendment referencing the quarterly invoicing schedule.
- Maintain standard pricing (no additional discount beyond the committed ARR pricing) unless finance wants to trade a financial concession.
- Approve Net-90 for the first two invoices (pilot), revert to Net-30 thereafter unless credit and usage metrics are met.
- Require a credit-check and consolidated invoice contact; billing will place account on conditional terms until the PO arrives.

I'm copying Laura and Karthik to request formal approval; Laure/Karthik, can you review below and advise if deal desk can approve the pilot with these guardrails? I have attached the current SOW and pricing quote for context.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec escalation: SpruceBridge — request Net-90 + quarterly invoices (details + recommendation)

Team — escalating for decision (deal desk + finance signoff). Summary and recommendation below.

External ask:
- SpruceBridge requests quarterly consolidated invoices with Net-90 payment terms for year-1 contract (estimated $180k ARR + $30k services).
- They will provide PO but need vendor payment window aligned to their fiscal cadence (quarterly).

Risk considerations:
- Cashflow impact: Net-90 increases DSO materially for a new account.
- Credit exposure: account is new to Redwood; we have not yet onboarded usage patterns.
- Operational: quarterly invoices increase billing reconciliation effort; billing supports but needs a PO up front.

Proposed mitigations (my recommended approvable structure):
1) Approve a 90-day invoice window for the first two quarters only (pilot). If customer meets payment SLAs and usage thresholds (no delinquency) by quarter 3, convert to Net-60 standard terms; otherwise revert to Net-30.
2) Accept quarterly consolidated invoices for the pilot, but require a customer PO and a signed SOW amendment before first invoice is issued.
3) No additional discounts beyond the quoted pricing in SB-pricing-quote-20260414.xlsx. If SpruceBridge seeks additional concession, require revenue protection clauses (e.g., shorten pilot or require advance partial payment).
4) Billing to run a credit-check; finance to approve conditional terms and flag account for weekly collections monitoring.
5) Require an escrow or ACH mandate if invoiced amount exceeds two consecutive unpaid invoices.

Requested decision: approval to offer the pilot structure above and to instruct legal to prepare a short amendment (quarterly invoicing schedule + Net-90 pilot clause). If approved, I will confirm terms back to Elena and request the PO.

Context: HubSpot deal SB-2026-087 contains current quote and SOW. I recommend approval to keep momentum; SpruceBridge signoff expected to close by end of April.

Thanks,
Vivek

-- attachment: credit-check-summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, billing@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec escalation: SpruceBridge — request Net-90 + quarterly invoices (decision)

Vivek / team — thanks for the clear recommendation and supporting docs. After reviewing the numbers and credit summary, we will approve a controlled pilot with the following conditions (please mirror these in the amendment):

1) Pilot duration: first two invoices only (covering Q2 and Q3). After that, terms revert to Net-30 unless finance confirms credit good standing.
2) PO and signed amendment required prior to provisioning. No exceptions.
3) No additional pricing concessions. If customer requests a discount in exchange for Net-90, that must come with a committed ARR uplift or prepayment tranche.
4) Billing to mark invoices as "conditional" and Billing Ops will initiate weekly aging reports to the collections mailbox.

Action items: Vivek — send Elena the amendment template and request PO; Legal will prepare the short DocuSign amendment (I copied billing & Priyom for tracking). Priyom — please confirm billing can operationalize the conditional flag and collections cadence.

Approve: Karthik Iyer, VP Sales — on behalf of the deal desk

-- signature: Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
